cohort: The study included 3,416,517 births from 2013 to 2022 covered by the Korean National Health Insurance Service.
finding: Less than one-fifth of the increase in the cesarean delivery rate from 2013 to 2022 in South Korea was explained by changes in maternal age, parity, multiple births, residential area, and income level, suggesting other diverse factors are driving the trend.
mod_finding: The cesarean delivery rate increased from 37.8% in 2013 to 61.6% in 2022, with maternal age structure contributing only 8.7% to this increase and other demographic and socioeconomic factors collectively explaining less than one-fifth.
